messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — staging saw a ~40% tail-latency spike for small-batch decode requests after the FlashAttention variant toggle yesterday. attaching profiler snippet and a short trace.

sam: Yup, noticed it in the dashboard around 14:02 PT. Not all kernels regressed, looks specific to the 'fused-paged' path when sequence_len < 8.

kevin: Can you paste the short profiler output? I want to see where the GPU is stalling.

maria: Paste below — this is from a 128-concurrent small-decoder workload (1-4 tokens) on an a100: 
```
CPU: scheduling jitter ~0.8ms
GPU kernels:
  launch_kernel_fused_paged(...)  45.2%
  kvcache_refill_prefill_path     22.7% (many syncs)
  flash_attn_variant_fallback    12.1%
  other                           20%
```
Observation: fused_paged path does extra syncs for tiny seqs, causing poor small-batch util.

iris: Interesting — IIRC fused-paged introduced a microkernel that assumes larger tile widths. When sequence_len small, it issues an extra memcpy or barrier.

leo: I reproduced with local bench: single-token decode QPS drops 30% and tail gets worse under continuous batching.

sam: Hypothesis: kernel selection heuristics shifted weights towards fused-paged for low sequence lengths after we tuned for long-prefill throughput. The selector cost model didn't account for micro-launch overhead.

kevin: Agreed. Two quick fixes to try: 1) add a cheap fast-path rule: if decode && seq_len <= 8 && batch_size <= 8 => prefer small-decode kernel. 2) add amortized launch overhead into selector cost. Which is faster to test?

maria: Fast-path rule should be trivial and low-risk. I'll patch selector.cpp and run the staging canary.

devops-bot: Canary deploy queued: canary-788 -> eng-runtime-staging (tag: kernel-hotfix-2263). ETA 6m.

leo: Also let's enable KV warmup tracing for this canary — I suspect kvcache refill is doing synchronous pages for decode hotpaths.

maria: Good call. Enabling vmmap tracing + kv stats. Patch: 
```diff
- if (candidate == fused_paged) cost = estimate(candidate);
+ if (candidate == fused_paged && is_decode && seq_len <= 8 && batch_size <= 8) {
+   cost += LARGE_PENALTY; // prefer small-decode kernel for tiny workloads
+ }
```
I'll push in 10m.

sam: Please add an opt-in runtime flag so we can roll back without redeploying the selector binary. "--prefer-small-decode-for-tiny" or similar.

maria: good idea, will add flag.

kevin: After the canary, let's run microbench for the boundary conditions (seq_len 1..16, batch 1..16) and produce a 2D heatmap of latency delta between fused-paged vs small-decode. I can script that.

iris: Also trace GPU occupancy and kernel launch counts. If occupancy low but launch count high, that's the anti-pattern.

leo: FYI I also saw a related regression on a different commit where continuous-batching scheduler raised max microbatch to 12 for decode, which interacts badly here. Might be two factors multiplying.

maria: noted. I'll coordinate with scheduler owners to revert microbatch cap if canary doesn't help.

devops-bot: Canary deploy succeeded: canary-788 -> eng-runtime-staging (status: healthy).

sam: Early canary numbers look promising — tail down ~22% on the synthetic small-decoder job. Can we run a longer soak?

maria: Running 30m soak with KV tracing. Leaving it on prod-like load.

leo: Attached flamegraph (short link): https://internal.srv/fg/2263-smallbatch-fix — shows fused_paged kernel excluded for tiny paths now.

kevin: Great. If soak passes, let's gate a prod rollout but include the selector flag default-on for next week. Also include a perf regression test in the CI matrix: tiny-seq decode microbenchmark.

iris: One more ask — update the kernel docs to list the empirical breakpoints. This will save future surprises.

maria: Will do. I have a draft metrics table I'll upload to the runbook.

sam: Postmortem-ish note: we tuned selector for big-prefill throughput but forgot to validate decode microcases. Lesson: add targeted microbench in release checklist.

maria: Agree. Thanks all. I'll follow up with PR link and soak results later. :thumbsup:

kevin: Thx — ping me when PR is up so I can review the selector heuristics.

maria: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4512 (branch: hotstart-small-decode-2263)

leo: LGTM on the change; tests pass locally.

maria: Closing loop — canary soak passed 30m, prod rollout scheduled, and CI microbench added. Will open runbook entry after prod verification.

devops-bot: Prod rollout scheduled for 2:00 UTC.

sam: Nice job team.

maria: Thanks. I'll leave the KV traces in logs for 24h and then purge.

leo: We'll revisit if anything else pops up.

(END)
